messages:
maria: Quick q — for private VPC customers with egress disabled to internet, what's expected behavior for smart routing fallback? e.g. if the preferred model variant in region A is out of capacity, do we route to a variant in another region or to a local smaller/quantized variant? Need a clear control-plane policy for compliance customers. :thinking:
kevin: Short answer: we should NOT cross the customer's VPC/network boundary if their egress policy forbids it. We have two main modes in practice: regional_only and cross_region_fallback, but the semantics for model-variant fallback are fuzzy.
maria: Got it. Is regional_only currently enforced for Private tenants by default?
kevin: Yes, for new Private enrollments the control plane defaults to regional_only. Older tenants might have cross_region_fallback enabled. Ops has been conservative.
anya: Runtime note: we can fall back to a locally-compiled quantized variant (example: q4_k_mixed) if it's present in the same region/tenant pool. Autoconversion or on-the-fly quantization is not something we do on private clusters today. That limits 'local fallback' to pre-provisioned variants.
sam: Security brief: if egress=false at tenant-level, control plane must not instruct data plane to call external endpoints or other regions. Even offloading to a partner region within the same org is suspect unless explicitly allowed. We need telemetry that proves no cross-network egress happened. :lock:
tina: Console/UX — we need an explicit badge in Rollouts and Routes: e.g. "Cross-region fallback: disabled". Also show telemetry that indicates attempts blocked due to egress. That helps SREs and product owners.
kevin: Proposal: default for Private = regional_only. Add two opt-ins: (1) explicit cross-region-fallback via signed contract/SLO, (2) local-variant-fallback when tenant pre-populates quantized variants. For clarity, config could look like:
```
routing:
  mode: regional_only  # options: regional_only, cross_region_fallback
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1]  # used only in cross-region mode
  allow_model_variant_fallback: true  # allows switching to pre-provisioned local variants
```
kevin: With that, control plane enforcement logic: if mode==regional_only and no local variant available => return 409/EGRESS_BLOCKED to the caller so app can handle gracefully.
maria: If we return 409, customers will likely retry. Can we offer an in-console retry suggestion or fallback to a small local stub model?
anya: We can provide a "stub" policy: if pre-provisioned tiny models exist (e.g., local-distill-128), runtime can route there with clear flag. But we must ensure quality/regression monitoring warns product owners — output will differ.
sam: Telemetry requirement: every decision must be logged. Add field egress_decision with values: blocked|fallback_local|fallback_cross_region. Also include decision_reason and policy_version. Retain at least 90 days for audit tenants.
ops-bot: policy-checker: staging policy applied to tenant-42: routing.mode=regional_only — 17 violations detected in last 24h (requests tried to cross-region).
policy-checker: suggestion: surface top callers causing violations in console and add per-route opt-out warnings.
tina: UX microcopy idea for Rollouts page: "Cross-region fallback disabled by tenant policy — contact account admin to enable for controlled emergency bursts." We'll add a tooltip that links to audit logs. :memo:
kevin: Dev plan: I'll open a PR that enforces the routing.mode at control-plane response time, returns 409 + body {"code":"EGRESS_BLOCKED","policy":"regional_only","policy_version":"v2"} for blocked requests, and emits egress_decision metadata. Also add integration tests: matrix of (private/no-egress x model-availability) -> expected behavior (blocked | fallback_local).
maria: Billing question: if we fallback to a smaller local variant, token cost changes. Need billing attribution and an explicit flag in telemetry to record billed_model_variant and billed_token_multiplier.
sam: Agreed — security & finance need that. Also ensure logs don't leak model internals or prompt contents in audit exports.
anya: Implementation note for runtime headers: add X-Redwood-Egress-Decision and include decision_reason in response headers for observability. For blocked: X-Redwood-Egress-Decision: blocked; reason=EGRESS_POLICY_REGIONAL_ONLY.
tina: I'll mock the console flows and show a dashboard line chart that separates blocked vs fallback_local vs allowed. Also add a per-tenant alert rule template: ">5 egress_blocked per minute => page oncall".
kevin: One more: rollout UX for changing mode should require an explicit checkbox and a justification field for Private tenants, and should kick off an automatic security review for cross_region_fallback opt-ins.
maria: Thanks — can someone own the rollout doc and SOC signoff checklist? I can coordinate with product.
sam: I'll own SOC signoff. I'll create a short doc with telemetry fields, retention, and required contract language.
kevin: I'll attach PR link in this thread when ready and tag infra for test matrix runs. :rocket:
maria: Perfect, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with stakeholder list and timeline. :thumbsup:
